title: HPC Digital Twins for Evaluating Scheduling Policies, Incentive Structures and their Impact on Power and Cooling
problem: Evaluating scheduler policies and their physical infrastructure impact is limited to post-deployment analysis or simulators that don't model infrastructure. Need way to evaluate scheduler impact on power, cooling, and sustainability before deployment.
motivation: Enable what-if scenarios to evaluate scheduler policies and their impact on physical infrastructure (power, cooling, sustainability) before production deployment.
method: The researchers created a digital twin—a computer simulation that accurately mimics real high-performance computing (HPC) systems—and extended it to evaluate different scheduling policies (the rules that decide which jobs run when). Using real operational data from actual supercomputers as input, the simulation can predict how changes to scheduling would affect power consumption and cooling needs. The framework connects to external scheduling simulators and can test scenarios with financial incentive structures and machine-learning-based scheduling algorithms.
key_novelty: The core innovation is pairing HPC scheduling simulators with digital twins to predict how scheduling changes affect power and cooling before deploying them to real systems.
contributions: First digital twin framework with scheduling capabilities
Integration of publicly available datasets from top-tier HPC systems
Extensions for external scheduling simulator integration
Incentive structure implementation in digital twins
What-if scenario methodology for sustainability evaluation

metrics.primary: Scheduler impact on power consumption and cooling

limitations: Abstract does not provide specific performance or sustainability metrics. Focus appears to be on framework rather than quantitative results.
primary_theme: Digital Twin-Based HPC Scheduling and Infrastructure Optimization
